label: Gmail
seoTitle: Gmail Email Signature Generator | Setup and Troubleshooting Guide
metaDescription: Create a Gmail email signature, install it in Gmail settings, and fix image, spacing, mobile, and dark-mode problems with this practical guide.
heading: Gmail Email Signature Generator
description: Build a professional Gmail signature, paste it into Gmail Settings, and test it before relying on it for client or customer email. This guide focuses on Gmail's signature defaults, hosted images, mobile overrides, and dark-mode behaviour.
installInstructions: Create and preview your signature in the email signature generator.
Use Copy for Gmail to copy the rich HTML version.
In Gmail on the web, select the gear icon, then See all settings.
In the Signature section, create a signature or select the one you want to replace.
Click in the editor and paste with Cmd+V or Ctrl+V.
Choose that signature as the default for new emails and for replies or forwards, then select Save Changes.
Send a test message and run the finished HTML through the signature health check.

guideSections.heading: Set Gmail defaults after you paste
paragraphs: Gmail's signature editor accepts pasted rich HTML, but it is not a web page editor. It keeps simple inline table layouts, links, images, colours, and basic typography, then removes markup it does not support. Use the generator's rich HTML copy rather than rebuilding the design in Gmail.

Creating a signature is not enough on its own. Set it as the default for both new messages and replies or forwards, then save the page. If either dropdown still says No signature, your new block can look as though it was never saved.
items: Paste directly into Gmail rather than through a plain-text notes app.
Use a short reply signature if long email threads are common.
Send a test email to a separate inbox after every material edit.
Keep contact links as normal text links so they remain useful when images are blocked.

guideSections.heading: Use reliable images and simple HTML
paragraphs: An image that lives only on your computer cannot load for recipients. Use a stable HTTPS image URL for a logo or photo, give important images explicit dimensions, and include meaningful alt text. The signature should still make sense when an inbox blocks remote images.

Gmail is most dependable with tables and inline styles. Avoid external CSS, base64 images, and decorative techniques that depend on browser layout behaviour. If the exact image crop matters to your brand, test the sent signature in more than one email client.
items: Use compressed logos and photos that stay legible at small sizes.
Avoid relying on transparent artwork as the only visible brand element.
Do not use a local file path as an image source.
Review the signature examples before simplifying an overloaded layout.

guideSections.heading: Check mobile and dark mode separately
paragraphs: The Gmail mobile app can use a separate mobile signature. If that field contains older text, Gmail may append it or show it instead of the HTML signature configured on desktop. Check the setting for the same account after you save the web version.

Gmail dark mode can recolour text or backgrounds. Strong contrast, visible links, and a signature that does not depend on transparent backgrounds make the result more resilient. The health check helps catch contrast and client-specific concerns before you send important mail.
items: Update or disable Gmail's separate mobile signature override.
Avoid low-contrast grey text as the only contact treatment.
Open the test message in Gmail on desktop and mobile.
Use the health check after changes to colours, logos, or trackers.

troubleshooting.fix: Copy the rich HTML version again, click directly inside Gmail's signature editor, and paste with Cmd+V or Ctrl+V. Do not paste through a plain-text editor.
Confirm the image URL begins with https:// and opens in a private browser window. If it only opens on your computer or company network, recipients cannot load it.
Return to Gmail Settings and assign the signature as the default for new messages and replies or forwards before saving changes.

troubleshooting.issue: The mobile app shows an old signature
troubleshooting.fix: Open Gmail mobile settings for that account and update or disable the separate mobile signature.

additionalFaqs.q: Why does Gmail change my signature colours in dark mode?
additionalFaqs.a: Gmail may recolour text and backgrounds so messages remain readable in dark inboxes. Transparent backgrounds, pure black text, and low-contrast greys are more likely to change, so test the finished signature before publishing it.

additionalFaqs.q: Can I use the same Gmail signature in Google Workspace?
additionalFaqs.a: The same signature can be used in Gmail for personal accounts and Google Workspace accounts. If an administrator manages signatures centrally, follow that policy before replacing the individual signature.

additionalFaqs.q: Why is my Gmail signature image an attachment?
additionalFaqs.a: This commonly happens when a signature uses a local image or pasted image blob instead of a hosted HTTPS image URL. Use a hosted image URL and paste the full HTML signature.

label: Outlook
seoTitle: Outlook Email Signature Generator | Setup and Rendering Guide
metaDescription: Create an Outlook email signature and install it in Outlook for Windows, Mac, and the web with practical rendering, image, and spacing advice.
heading: Email Signature Generator for Outlook
description: Create an Outlook signature with conservative, email-safe HTML, then set it up in the Outlook version you use. This guide covers web, Windows, and Mac settings, image handling, default signatures, and the layout limits of classic Outlook for Windows.
installInstructions: Create and preview the signature in the email signature generator.
Copy the rich HTML version with Copy for Gmail; the same table-based HTML can be pasted into Outlook.
In Outlook on the web or new Outlook for Windows, open Settings, then Mail and Compose and reply.
In classic Outlook for Windows, use File, Options, Mail, then Signatures. In Outlook for Mac, use Outlook, Settings, then Signatures.
Create or select a signature, paste into the editor, save it, and select defaults for new messages and replies or forwards.
Send a test email to Gmail and Apple Mail, then use the signature health check to review the HTML.

guideSections.heading: Find the right Outlook signature settings
paragraphs: Outlook has several interfaces, so the setting location depends on which one you use. Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows place it in Settings, Mail, Compose and reply. Classic Outlook for Windows uses File, Options, Mail, Signatures, while Outlook for Mac has its own Signatures settings.

After creating the HTML block, choose it as the default for new messages and replies or forwards. Outlook can store several signatures, which means a valid signature can still fail to appear if the default dropdowns are left unset.
items: Use Outlook on the web for a clean paste if classic Outlook changes spacing.
Set new-message and reply defaults separately.
Keep a shorter reply signature for long conversations.
Send test messages to multiple clients before a team-wide rollout.

guideSections.heading: Design for classic Outlook on Windows
paragraphs: Classic Outlook for Windows uses Microsoft Word to render messages, so browser layout techniques can fail even if they look correct in a preview. Flexbox, grid, external style sheets, advanced positioning, and background images are particularly fragile.

A table-based layout with inline styles, fixed image dimensions, and simple spacing is more dependable. Keep the signature readable with images blocked, and use familiar fonts rather than depending on a font installed only on your own machine.
items: Use tables rather than flexbox or CSS grid.
Keep styling inline instead of in a style block.
Avoid background images and absolute positioning.
Use publicly reachable HTTPS images with explicit dimensions.

guideSections.heading: Prepare a signature for teams and Microsoft 365
paragraphs: For an individual, adding the generated HTML in Outlook settings is enough. For a small team, test one approved layout across the Outlook versions in use, then duplicate it with each person's contact details. This keeps logo sizes, colours, and links consistent without asking everyone to redesign the signature.

If a Microsoft 365 administrator manages signatures centrally, use the tested HTML as the approved layout and follow the administrator's distribution process. A centrally managed signature may replace individual settings, so confirm the chosen policy before staff make local changes.
items: Test the shared layout in Outlook desktop and web first.
Keep legal text short so it does not bury contact details in replies.
Use hosted images that work outside a company network.
Document the exact links and colour values used in the approved layout.

troubleshooting.fix: Paste the table-based HTML and avoid rebuilding spacing inside Outlook. Manual edits can add Word-specific markup that changes row heights.
Use publicly reachable HTTPS image URLs with explicit width and height. Confirm the image itself loads outside your logged-in browser.

troubleshooting.issue: The signature works on web but not desktop
troubleshooting.fix: Classic Outlook for Windows is stricter than Outlook on the web. Remove browser-only layout techniques and recreate the signature with a simple table-based layout.
Create a shorter reply signature with only the name, role, phone number, and website, while keeping the fuller version for new conversations.

additionalFaqs.q: Why does Outlook break HTML signatures more often than Gmail?
additionalFaqs.a: Classic Outlook for Windows renders messages with Microsoft Word rather than a browser engine. Modern layout CSS can fail there even when the same signature looks correct in Gmail or Apple Mail, so table-based HTML with inline styles is safer.

additionalFaqs.q: Does this work with Outlook 365 and Outlook.com?
additionalFaqs.a: The generated signature can be pasted into Outlook on the web, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365, new Outlook for Windows, classic Outlook for Windows, and Outlook for Mac. Test the specific desktop and web versions your team uses.

additionalFaqs.q: Should I include a long legal disclaimer in Outlook?
additionalFaqs.a: Include a disclaimer only when your role, industry, or employer requires it. Long disclaimers add weight to every thread and can bury useful contact details, so keep required text concise and approved.

label: Apple Mail
seoTitle: Apple Mail Email Signature Generator | Mac Setup Guide
metaDescription: Create an Apple Mail email signature, set it up on Mac, and test image, font, iPhone, and dark-mode compatibility with this practical guide.
heading: Email Signature Generator for Apple Mail
description: Build an Apple Mail signature, paste it into the Mac signature editor, and test it in sent email before you rely on it. This guide covers the macOS editor, message-font settings, iPhone and iPad expectations, hosted images, and dark-mode compatibility.
installInstructions: Create and preview the signature in the email signature generator.
Copy the rich HTML version with Copy for Gmail.
Open Mail on your Mac, then choose Mail, Settings, and Signatures.
Select the account, add or choose a signature, and turn off Always match my default message font before you paste.
Click inside the editor and paste with Cmd+V, then choose the signature for new messages and replies if you use different defaults.
Send a message to Gmail or Outlook, then use the signature health check to review the finished HTML.

guideSections.heading: Use the macOS signature editor without flattening the design
paragraphs: Apple Mail has a native signature editor for each account. Before pasting rich HTML, disable Always match my default message font; otherwise Mail can replace the intended font treatment with your compose font. Paste into the selected signature editor and set the relevant defaults after the content is in place.

Keep the design simple enough to survive forwarding and replies. Tables, inline styles, and a clear text-first contact block are safer than decorative layout tricks. If Mail changes the pasted content, copy the generated rich HTML again and avoid editing it through a plain-text app.
items: Select the correct sending account before creating the signature.
Disable the default-message-font option before pasting.
Use separate new-message and reply defaults when needed.
Send a test before deleting an older working signature.

guideSections.heading: Plan for iPhone and iPad separately
paragraphs: The Mail app on iPhone and iPad uses its own signature setting. A signature configured in Mail on a Mac does not automatically become the mobile signature for every account. Treat the mobile setting as a separate decision: use a compact text version, or leave it disabled if you do not want it appended to messages.

When a recipient opens your message on mobile, the important test is whether your name, role, contact details, and links remain easy to use. Avoid wide rows, tiny text, and information that only appears in an image.
items: Review Settings, Apps, Mail, Signature on iPhone or iPad for the sending account.
Keep the mobile version shorter than a desktop brand signature.
Make phone numbers and websites easy to tap.
Test a sent message in both portrait and dark mode.

guideSections.heading: Keep images and colours reliable in Apple Mail
paragraphs: Use hosted HTTPS URLs for photos and logos, rather than local file paths. Give important images sensible dimensions and alt text, and make sure the text contact block stands on its own when an inbox blocks remote images.

Apple Mail can display a broad range of formatting, but recipients may read the same message in Gmail or Outlook. Test with a dark background as well as a light background, keep contrast strong, and use the health check if you change colours or tracking links.
items: Use stable HTTPS image URLs and compressed assets.
Avoid transparent logos that disappear against a dark background.
Use normal text links for core contact actions.
Review the signature examples for layouts that stay compact on mobile.

troubleshooting.issue: Apple Mail changes the font after paste
troubleshooting.fix: In Mail Settings, Signatures, turn off Always match my default message font before pasting the rich HTML version again.

troubleshooting.issue: The signature appears in one account but not another
troubleshooting.fix: Apple Mail stores signatures by sending account. Select the intended account in Mail Settings, Signatures, then set that signature as the default for the account.

troubleshooting.issue: My iPhone still adds old text
troubleshooting.fix: Update or disable the separate Mail signature in iPhone or iPad settings. The mobile signature is configured independently from the Mac version.
Replace any local or private image source with a publicly reachable HTTPS URL, and confirm it loads outside your logged-in browser.

additionalFaqs.q: Why does Apple Mail change my signature font?
additionalFaqs.a: Apple Mail can apply the account's default message font when Always match my default message font is enabled. Turn that option off before pasting the rich HTML signature.

additionalFaqs.q: Will my Mac signature automatically appear on iPhone?
additionalFaqs.a: No. The Mail signature on iPhone and iPad is configured separately, so check the mobile setting for the account you use to send messages.

additionalFaqs.q: How should I test an Apple Mail signature?
additionalFaqs.a: Send a test message from Apple Mail to Gmail and Outlook, check it on a phone if that matters to your recipients, and confirm logos, links, spacing, and contrast still work.
